finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-controlled Base64 data directly to Marshal.load, allowing insecure deserialization that leads to remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: params[:state] — form/query parameter on public POST /restore (Sinatra default binding, no authentication)

trace.note: post "/restore" route is a public ingress with no auth filter
params[:state] is Base64-decoded and passed to Marshal.load, which instantiates arbitrary objects
state.inspect is returned, but gadget chains execute during load, before this line

finding.guards_checked: No authentication/authorization, no signature/HMAC on the payload, no class allowlist, no before filter, and no Rack middleware in the app. The only decoding is Base64, which is not a control. Sinatra's rack-protection does not block this.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 shows a public POST /restore that passes Base64-decoded params[:state] straight to Marshal.load, with no auth, signature, or class allowlist anywhere in the single-file app, so an anonymous attacker can trigger unsafe deserialization.
